verdict.rationale: Keycloak is precisely designed to act as an OAuth2/OIDC provider: developers register clients (third-party apps), Keycloak issues access/refresh tokens via standard endpoints, supports dynamic client registration, introspection, revocation, and client-credentials/service-account flows, effectively letting any app become the OAuth provider for other clients. Docs show client registration, well-known config, and token endpoints in depth. missing for 10: independent hands-on verification of a developer specifically exposing their own app as a third-party OAuth provider (all evidence is first-party docs plus general community sentiment, not a concrete 'sign in with my app' walkthrough).
